investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only. All retained evidence acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion, real descriptive User-Agent) against the venue's own official domain: the bare https://sagrescampopequeno.pt and https://sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/agenda (both confirmed as clean 301 redirects to the canonical https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt host), the resulting https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/ homepage, the candidate https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/agenda events page (verified as the correct, live, current agenda page), four sampled event detail pages reached from that agenda page's own links (alphaville, megadeth, the-nutcracker-ice-show, brandi-carlile---cancelado — deliberately including one already-cancelled listing to observe how the source itself signals cancellation), one additional fetch of an event's short canonical URL form to empirically cross-check slug stability across two distinct URL shapes, and the site's own publicly disclosed robots.txt + sitemap_index.xml + pt/sitemap.xml. Inspected the retained HTML for JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent data (none found anywhere — only a standard BreadcrumbList block on both list and detail pages), ICS/RSS export links (none found), and known calendar-plugin/CMS fingerprints (none found — the Server header identifies a bespoke 'nuvem server/5.0' platform, not WordPress/Squarespace/EventOn; no <meta name="generator"> tag present). Found instead a plain, fully server-rendered event list (28 distinct event cards, each with title/local/date directly in the raw HTML, no JS execution needed) and plain, fully server-rendered event detail pages (each with a full date+weekday, venue name, start/doors time, and a multi-tier admission price list, all directly in the raw HTML). robots.txt discloses a 'Disallow: /api' path; per policy this was deliberately NOT probed (no reason existed to escalate past a site's own stated preference when Level 1 static HTML already fully answers every question this investigation needed to answer). A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed all retained HTML/XML files to mechanically re-derive every claim below, including a real Gregorian-calendar cross-check (year/month/day taken from each sampled event's own stated date text, never from today's real-world date) confirming all 4 sampled events' self-stated Portuguese weekday names are internally consistent, and an empirical cross-check that the same event's canonical short URL and agenda-relative URL serve identical content. Level 1 was SUFFICIENT; no escalation to Level 2/3/4 was attempted.
investigator.notes: The prior loose lead in sources/lisbon.json (research_notes: 'Plain HTML list with dated acts confirmed into 2027', monitoring_status READY_FOR_TECHNICAL_PROOF) was treated only as a discovery lead, not as evidence. This investigation independently re-fetched and re-verified everything from its own retained evidence; sources/lisbon.json itself was never read as authority and was never modified.

probe_history.reason: Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of the bare domain, the www homepage, the candidate agenda page, four sampled event detail pages, one canonical-URL-form cross-check, robots.txt, and two sitemap files all returned 200 OK (the two bare-domain requests returned clean 301 redirects to the canonical www host, which were followed). The agenda page's raw, unrendered HTML already contained ALL 28 currently-listed events as fully server-rendered cards (title + city + date, each with its own detail-page link) with no JS execution needed — confirmed by mechanically parsing all 28 cards directly from the retained static file. Each of the 4 sampled event detail pages likewise contained its own full date+weekday, exact venue name, start/doors time, and a multi-tier admission price list, all directly in the raw server-rendered HTML. No JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent data was found anywhere (only a standard BreadcrumbList block), no ICS/RSS link was found, and the Server header ('nuvem server/5.0') and absence of any generator meta tag or WordPress/Squarespace/EventOn fingerprint indicate a bespoke CMS, not a recognisable off-the-shelf calendar plugin. This already answers identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field assessment for a genuine forward-dated concert calendar (28 events spanning September 2026 through June 2027, matching the prior loose note's 'confirmed into 2027' claim) without needing to inspect JS bundles or open a browser, so escalation to Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) or beyond was not attempted.

venue_reference: Campo Pequeno (Sagres Campo Pequeno) — large multi-use arena/bullring venue, Avenida da República, Campo Pequeno, Lisboa, Portugal (stated capacity 100 to 9,000 people, shared with a shopping centre in the same historic building)

identity.notes: Independently re-confirmed by this investigation's own retained evidence, not assumed from the prior loose registry note. The bare domain given in sources/lisbon.json (https://sagrescampopequeno.pt) 301-redirects to https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/, whose own retained HTML <title> is 'Sagres Campo Pequeno' and whose meta description states 'O Sagres Campo Pequeno como espaço multiusos permite receber espectáculos e eventos com a participação de 100 a 9 mil pessoas' — a first-person description of exactly the well-known real venue (the Campo Pequeno bullring/arena in Lisbon). The homepage repeatedly self-identifies as 'Sagres Campo Pequeno' (page title, meta title/description/og/twitter tags, footer section heading) and states its own street context 'com entrada principal pela Avenida da República' (main entrance via Avenida da República) — matching the registry's physical_address neighbourhood. The candidate agenda page shares the same canonical www domain and the same site-wide header/footer branding. No full postal code or a complete multi-line postal address was found in the retained evidence (only the street/avenue context and 'Campo Pequeno, Lisboa'), which is recorded honestly as a minor gap, not smoothed over — consistent with how the fama-dalfama-lisbon-01 investigation handled the same kind of partial-address situation.

site_classification.platform: A bespoke, non-WordPress CMS (Server header 'nuvem server/5.0'; no <meta name="generator"> tag; no WordPress/Squarespace/EventOn/The-Events-Calendar fingerprint found anywhere in the retained HTML). The agenda listing and every event detail page are plain, fully server-rendered HTML — no client-side rendering, no hidden data blob, no JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent structured data (only a standard BreadcrumbList JSON-LD block on both list and detail pages). robots.txt discloses a 'Disallow: /api' path and a sitemap at /sitemap_index.xml; the /api path was deliberately not probed since Level 1 static HTML already fully answered every field this investigation needed and there was no justification to escalate past a site's own stated crawl preference.

XML_SITEMAP (corroborating evidence for canonical-slug stability only — NOT itself the primary data path; observed to contain at least one stale/no-longer-listed event slug, so it must never be treated as an authoritative 'currently on sale' list)

REST_API_PATH (disclosed via robots.txt's 'Disallow: /api' line — deliberately NOT probed; Level 1 static HTML already fully answered this investigation, and there was no justification to escalate past the site's own stated crawl preference for an unneeded path)

title.notes: Representative value taken from the 'alphaville' sample event (this field's general extraction capability, not one single event, is the real finding — see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for every other sampled value). Every event's title is stated directly and in full, twice over: once in the agenda-list card's own <h3 class="card-title"> (e.g. 'Alphaville', 'Rui Veloso Trio', 'Titãs', 'MEO COMMEDIA À LA CARTE FEST'26 - REBENTA A BOLHA') and again, identically, in the detail page's own <h1> (e.g. 'Alphaville', 'Megadeth', 'The Nutcracker Ice Show', 'Brandi Carlile - cancelado'). Verified mechanically: all 28/28 agenda cards have a non-empty title, and all 4/4 sampled detail pages have a non-empty <h1> title (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt).

start_date.notes: Representative value taken from the 'alphaville' sample event, stated on the source as '16 outubro 2026 , sexta-feira' (day + Portuguese month name + year + weekday, all in one directly-stated string — see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the other 3 sampled events' values). Every event's full calendar date is stated directly and completely in one place, on both the agenda-list card (e.g. '16 outubro 2026') and the detail page's own header block, which additionally states the Portuguese weekday name — this is a single, complete, directly-stated fact, not a combination of separate context pieces, so basis is DIRECT_SOURCE rather than DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT. Cross-checked mechanically and NOT merely trusted: for all 4 sampled detail pages, the date matches the corresponding agenda-card date exactly (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt), and evidence/offline-proof.mjs independently recomputes, using pure Gregorian calendar arithmetic (year/month/day taken from each event's OWN stated date text, never from today's real-world date or any external assumption), the real day-of-week for each of the 4 sampled dates and confirms all 4/4 match the source's own stated weekday name exactly ('16 outubro 2026' independently confirmed to be a real-world Friday). This is a floating local date — no explicit UTC offset or IANA timezone is stated anywhere in the retained HTML; Europe/Lisbon is the obvious real-world timezone but this was never promoted to a fabricated UTC instant.

time.notes:
Every sampled detail page's 'Sessões' tab does state both a start time ('Início de espetáculo') and a doors time ('Abertura de portas'), in free text — but the retained fixtures show this free text is NOT in a single consistent format across events: 3 of the 4 sampled events use 'Início de espetáculo: HH H MM
Abertura de portas: HH H MM' (uppercase H, colon, start-then-doors order), while the 4th (megadeth) uses 'Abertura de Portas HHhMM
Inicio do Espetáculo HHhMM' (lowercase h, no colon, doors-then-start order, 'Inicio' without its accent). This inconsistency was mechanically confirmed, not merely suspected: evidence/offline-proof.mjs implements both patterns and reports the exact distribution found (3 pattern-A, 1 pattern-B in this 4-event sample). A collector needs to handle at least 2 free-text variants reliably, and this bounded sample cannot rule out further variants across the other 24 unsampled events — so this is honestly recorded as PARTIAL (a value genuinely exists and is extractable per-event with enough parsing effort) rather than PROVEN (which would overclaim a single robust, source-documented format).

end.notes: No end time or duration is stated anywhere in the retained agenda page or any of the 4 sampled event detail pages (the 'Sessões' tab states only a start time and a doors-opening time, never an end/finish time).

venue_location.notes:
Every one of the 4 sampled event detail pages states, directly and identically, '
Lisboa - Sagres Campo Pequeno
' in its own header block — the full venue name, not merely the city. This is a stronger, more precise statement than the agenda-list card's own '
Lisboa
' (city only, mechanically confirmed present on all 28/28 cards but never more precise than the city there). Verified mechanically for all 4/4 sampled detail pages (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt). No street address, postal code, or coordinates are exposed by this data path itself — those live only in this repository's own venues/manual-coordinates registry, which this investigation did not touch.

source_record_id.notes: Representative value: the 'alphaville' sample event's own canonical slug (see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the other 27 agenda-derived slugs, all distinct). The source's own URL slug (e.g. 'alphaville', 'megadeth', 'the-nutcracker-ice-show') is directly, explicitly declared as this event's canonical identifying path via its own <link rel="canonical" href="https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/{slug}"> tag on every sampled detail page — exactly the stable-identifier rule's own worked example ('a permalink URL slug the source uses as its own canonical path'). This was proven three independent ways, not merely asserted: (1) all 28 agenda-list cards link to a distinct /pt/agenda/{slug} with zero duplicate slugs (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt); (2) a second, independently-fetched source-authored artifact — the site's own retained pt/sitemap.xml — separately lists the identical /pt/{slug} canonical form for all 4 sampled events, corroborating the <link rel=canonical> tag rather than merely repeating it; (3) an empirical cross-fetch of the SAME event (alphaville) via its short canonical URL (https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/alphaville) returned the identical <h1> title and identical date+weekday text as the agenda-relative URL (https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/agenda/alphaville) fetched separately, proving both URL shapes resolve to the same underlying record under the same stable slug. This bounded 4-event sample did not happen to include any recurring/multi-date production sharing one slug across several distinct performance dates (the edge case flagged in this repository's own coliseu-ageas-porto-01 and gulbenkian-lisbon-01 investigations) — a future, larger sample should specifically check for that before treating source_record_id as unconditionally 1:1 with a single performance instance.

event_url.notes: Representative value: the 'alphaville' sample event's own canonical detail-page URL (see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the other 3 sampled events' canonical URLs). Every event has its own distinct, directly-stated, working detail-page URL: the agenda card's own href (https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/agenda/{slug}) and the detail page's own <link rel="canonical"> (https://www.sagrescampopequeno.pt/pt/{slug}) — both confirmed (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt) to resolve to 200 OK and to serve the same event content for the one event (alphaville) both forms were fetched for in this investigation. Unlike fama-dalfama-lisbon-01 (where all events shared one page URL), this source gives each event a genuinely distinct, per-event permalink.

price.value: Plateia VIP: 60€ | 1ª Plateia: 55€ | 2ª Plateia: 50€ | Bancada A: 55€ | Bancada B: 50€ | Bancada C (Vis. Reduzida): 45€ | Mobilidade Condicionada: 45€
price.notes: Representative value: the 'alphaville' sample event's full 7-tier price list, recorded as a single delimited string rather than a fabricated scalar (see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the other 3 sampled events' tier counts: megadeth 4, the-nutcracker-ice-show 9, brandi-carlile---cancelado 10, all retained pre-cancellation). Every one of the 4 sampled event detail pages states, directly, a full multi-tier admission price list in its own retained HTML: each <li data-areaname="..." data-price="...€"> gives a named seating/standing area and its exact euro price. Verified mechanically: all 4/4 sampled detail pages have at least one priced tier (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt). This is genuinely present and precisely stated, but it is fundamentally a STRUCTURED LIST of (area, price) pairs, not a single scalar 'the price' — a future collector/Offer model must represent multiple priced tiers per event (e.g. multiple Offer records, or an explicit min/max range), never compress it into one number without losing real information; the delimited-string value recorded here is a faithful transcription of the source's own tiers, not a synthesized single price.

blockers.description: The 'Sessões' tab's free-text start/doors time format is inconsistent across sampled events (2 distinct patterns found in a 4-event sample — see field_assessment.time.notes). A collector must implement and maintain multiple parsing patterns for this field, and this bounded sample cannot rule out further variants across the remaining ~24 unsampled events.

Price is exposed as a structured multi-tier list (named area + price per tier), not a single scalar. A collector/Offer model must represent multiple priced tiers per event rather than collapsing them into one number.

The source lists at least one already-cancelled event directly in its live public agenda (brandi-carlile---cancelado), signalled only by free text ('- cancelado' appended to the title; 'Evento Cancelado' inside the Sessões tab's own free text) — there is no distinct structured status/cancelled field. A collector must parse this textual convention to avoid presenting a cancelled show as an active, purchasable event; this investigation only confirmed the convention exists for this one sampled event and did not exhaustively search for other possible cancellation-signalling text variants.

The retained pt/sitemap.xml contains at least one event slug (jordan-b-peterson-an-evening-to-transform-your-life-cancelado) that is NOT present in the current /pt/agenda listing — the sitemap is useful corroborating evidence for slug stability but must never be treated as an authoritative 'currently on sale' event list; the live agenda page itself remains the authority for which events are currently listed.

This investigation's bounded 4-event sample did not include any recurring/multi-date production sharing one canonical slug across multiple distinct performance dates. A larger future sample should specifically check for that edge case (already observed in this repository's own coliseu-ageas-porto-01/gulbenkian-lisbon-01 investigations for other venues) before fully trusting source_record_id as unconditionally 1:1 with a single performance instance.

This independently re-verifies, rather than merely repeats, the prior loose research claim that this venue has 'a plain HTML list with dated acts confirmed into 2027' — this investigation's own retained evidence confirms 28 events spanning September 2026 through June 2027, genuinely as plain server-rendered HTML, without treating the prior note itself as evidence.
